title: Runtime evolution policy: compatibility signals, deprecation runway and automated migration helpers
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create and operationalize a runtime semantic versioning policy that combines explicit compatibility signals, a defined deprecation runway, and developer-facing migration helpers. The goal is to reduce consumer breakage during runtime evolution while enabling faster safe innovation in runtime-2.0.
background: We frequently run into late-stage consumer breakages when runtime internals or RPC fields change. Current ad-hoc deprecation notes and manual signaling are insufficient for the scale of clients using Hosted/Dedicated/Private modes. We need a reproducible policy and automation that: 1) defines what constitutes a breaking change vs safe extension, 2) surfaces compatibility risk in PRs and releases, 3) provides migration helpers (CLI + client adapters) to reduce friction, and 4) enforces rollout gates based on telemetry-driven risk.
design_decisions: 1) Introduce a four-tier compatibility classification: NONE (no change), ADDITIVE (safe extensions), BEHAVIORAL (changes that can alter semantics but can be feature-flagged), and BREAKING (must follow deprecation runway). 2) Add an authoritative compatibility header X-Redwood-Compat-Level and an Accept-Version header X-Redwood-Accept-Version for clients to opt into behavior. 3) Implement an automated api-diff job in CI that computes field-level diffs for runtime control-plane APIs and maps them to the classification heuristics. 4) Run deprecations for a minimum 90-day runway for BREAKING changes, with automated client-usage detection to extend runway when high-impact clients exist.
compatibility_scoring: We will compute a numeric 'compatibility_score' per change based on: schema churn (0-40), observed production usage of affected endpoints (0-30), frequency of field usage in cached KV (0-15), and historical consumer fragility (0-15). score >= 70 => BREAKING, 40-69 => BEHAVIORAL, 10-39 => ADDITIVE, <10 => NONE. The score and rationale will be surfaced in PR templates and the release notes.
migration_tooling: Deliver a migration-assistant CLI ('rw-migrate') that can: 1) run api-diff between two runtime bundles, 2) suggest minimal client adapter patches (JS/TS/Python), 3) generate compat shim server-side when possible, and 4) produce a 'consumer_impact_report' with top-5 affected customers. Also provide SDK adapters that implement Accept-Version fallback semantics and log structured telemetry events for automatic prioritization of customer outreach.
rollout_steps: 1) CI check: api-diff must be green or explicitly acknowledged in PR. 2) Canaries: release to internal traffic then 5% external with compat telemetry monitoring for 72 hours. 3) Automated gate: if compat.error_rate > 0.5% or consumer_error_spike on a top-20 customer, automatically halt rollout and trigger rollback. 4) Deprecation flow: BREAKING changes must create a linked deprecation issue, schedule email + console banner, and open a migration task per high-impact customer.
monitoring_and_alerting: New telemetry metrics: compat.change_score (per release), compat.error_rate (5m/1h), compat.consumer_spike (per-customer 1h), and compat.migration_progress (per-customer). Alerts: P0 if compat.error_rate > 1% sustained for 30m on hosted API; P1 if top-10 customer affected with >0.5% spike. Integrate with Console to show per-route compat risk in release view.
QA_plan: 1) Add unit tests for api-diff heuristics with synthetic schemas. 2) E2E test: rw-migrate suggestions applied against sample third-party clients in CI matrix. 3) Create a staged chaos test that simulates a partial rollback and validates graceful Accept-Version fallbacks. 4) Include a manual verification checklist for front-line SREs for the first three runtime-2.0 releases.
acceptance_criteria:
- api-diff job running in CI and failing PRs with unacknowledged BREAKING changes.
- rw-migrate CLI produces actionable migration suggestions for 90% of BREAKING diffs in our sample corpus.
- Console shows compat.change_score on the release page for runtime-2.0.
- At least one successful canary release using the new automated gate with rollback executed in test.
- Documentation (docs.redwood.ai) describing compatibility tiers, acceptable changes, and developer guide published.

T2: Develop compatibility scoring library and unit tests
T3: Build rw-migrate MVP (JS + Python helpers)
T4: Extend runtime to emit Accept-Version/X-Redwood-Compat-Level headers
T5: Console UI: release view compat scoring card
T6: Create deprecation automation (issue generation + email + banner)
T7: Add telemetry metrics and PagerDuty runbook entries
T8: Run internal canary and document rollback playbook
